question.problem:
Consider the function $y=(\operatorname{tan}⁡x)^{x}.$ Its derivative is given by  

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=(\operatorname{tan}⁡x)^{x}\cdot g(x).
$$

Find the function $g(x).$
question.worked_solution:
We have the function 

$$
y=(\operatorname{tan}⁡x)^{x}.
$$

First, we take the natural logarithm of both sides:

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{ln}⁡y & =\operatorname{ln}⁡((\operatorname{tan}⁡x)^{x}) \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡y & =x\operatorname{ln}⁡(\operatorname{tan}⁡x)\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we differentiate both sides with respect to $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{ln}⁡y) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(x\operatorname{ln}⁡(\operatorname{tan}⁡x)) \\ \frac{1}{y}\cdot \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(x)\cdot (\operatorname{ln}⁡(\operatorname{tan}⁡x))+(x)\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{ln}⁡(\operatorname{tan}⁡x)) \\ \frac{1}{y}\cdot \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =1\cdot \operatorname{ln}⁡(\operatorname{tan}⁡x)+x\cdot (\frac{1}{\operatorname{tan}⁡x}\cdot {sec}^{2}⁡x) \\ \frac{1}{y}\cdot \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(\operatorname{tan}⁡x)+x\operatorname{csc}⁡x\operatorname{sec}⁡x\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we solve for $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =y(\operatorname{ln}⁡(\operatorname{tan}⁡x)+x\operatorname{csc}⁡x\operatorname{sec}⁡x)\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we substitute $y=(\operatorname{tan}⁡x)^{x}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =(\operatorname{tan}⁡x)^{x}(\operatorname{ln}⁡(\operatorname{tan}⁡x)+x\operatorname{csc}⁡x\operatorname{sec}⁡x)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $g(x)=\operatorname{ln}⁡(\operatorname{tan}⁡x)+x\operatorname{csc}⁡x\operatorname{sec}⁡x.$
